proposal.claim: ORIGIN. This is taken from reports/SCOUT.jsonl line 4 (codex, slug leveraged-binance-usd-m-perpetual-short-whose-collateral), but sign-flipped, and the flip is why it is proposed rather than the line itself. That line names the liquidated leveraged SHORT, force-bought back by the exchange's own IoC order once maintenance margin breaks. Standing opposite that payer means being long while the short base is crowded, and the state variable that identifies a crowded short base in this project's data is persistently negative funding - which is exactly the rule carry_funding_long, exactly the payer H0006's claim already named ('the leveraged bear, and the desk holding spot that needs protection now'), and H0006 is closed. Its twin is untested: the liquidated leveraged LONG, force-SOLD by the same engine, identified by the same state variable with the opposite sign. That is the payer here. Nothing else in the notebook is reachable, and I checked all eighteen rather than asserting it: lines 0, 5, 7, 8, 13, 14 and 17 are anchored to a wall-clock calendar (the quarterly delivery fixing, the Deribit and CME expiry hours, the 07:30-08:00 dual-investment window, the Monday 00:00 UTC liquidity-provider tier reset, jurisdiction offboarding deadlines, daily tournament resets) and neither TrialConfig nor SignalTrialConfig has a field that can name a date, an hour or a weekday; lines 1, 2, 6, 10, 11, 12 and 15 need series this project does not hold (the margin-tier announcement archive, BUSD-quoted panels, ADL notifications, leveraged-token NAV and rebalance stamps, copy-trade attribution, TWAP parent orders, the Index and Mark price series); line 9's outage signature is measurable from the panel's own gap structure but is a script over missing bars, not anything a config field can express; line 3's delisting settlement is already what KT-3 measured as a terminal multiple, at zero ledger rows. PARTIAL TEST, STATED PLAINLY. Line 4's mechanism proper needs the forced-order stream, liquidation prints and open interest in order to ATTRIBUTE a move to compulsory flow. This project holds none of them. What is reachable is only the state variable - the trailing mean settlement rate, which says the leveraged base is crowded and expensive - and never the forced flow itself. So this tests whether standing opposite a crowded leveraged long base THROUGH its unwind is paid; it cannot say whether the payment came from forced liquidation or from ordinary selling, and no result from it may be reported as if it could. WHO PAYS, AND WHY THEY KEEP DOING IT. Not the ordinary crowded long paying the eight-hourly coupon: that payer is H0002's, and H0002 is closed with six of nine symbols showing no positive cell anywhere in 972 trials. The payer here is the marginal leveraged long who added exposure while funding was already rich and who, when the crowd thins, does not get to choose his exit - the exchange closes him at whatever the book offers, in size, and each closure walks price into the next maintenance level. He keeps doing it because leverage is the entire reason to be on a perpetual rather than in spot, so the long base rebuilds after every flush; the venue's fee schedule and insurance fund are underwritten on the assumption that it will. H0007 named this same payer and was closed, but it was closed on the SHAPE and not on the payer: a scheduled depositor who defers a contribution changes the price at which money lands and does not stop the perpetual charging funding for holding it, so its gain survived only with include_funding false. The side that is PAID funding while it waits has never been asked. WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT RULE SHAPE AND NOT H0002'S GRID RE-CUT. This is checkable in two files and I checked it rather than asserting it. orc/eval/signal_rules.py builds entry and exit as two independent masks - rich = mean_rate >= enter_rate, thin = mean_rate < exit_rate - so the band [exit_rate, enter_rate) is a hold zone and exit_rate alone decides how long an episode lasts. configs/registry/H0002.json carries exit_rate = 5e-05 in its FIXED block, not in its grid: in every one of its 972 trials the short was flattened as soon as the trailing settlement mean fell below +0.005 percent per settlement, which is while funding was still POSITIVE - that is, before the crowd left. H0002 was therefore structurally never in the position during a de-crowding, on any cell, at any parameter. That is a property of its fixed block rather than of its numbers, so citing it is not trawling its results. This family inverts the exit: the threshold sits at or below zero, so the position opens on the same crowding condition H0002 used and is released only once the settlement rate has actually inverted and the shorts are the ones paying. H0002 harvested the coupon and left before the flow; this holds for the flow and treats the coupon as what pays for the wait. RISK, STATED BEFORE THE NUMBERS. A rich trailing rate identifies a crowded long base; it does not time its unwind, and funding is richest while price is still rising. This rule is therefore deliberately early, and being early is precisely where H0002 bled. That is why the stop is on the grid rather than fixed: with a stop, earliness is capped and the rule re-enters while crowding persists. The wager is that the unwind's magnitude exceeds the cost of being early, and it is a wager, not a claim. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ENUMERATED. The unstopped corner: H0002 already recorded that a short with stop_loss null and max_hold_days null reaches -1.0, and re-running it would spend ledger rows to reconfirm a fact the ledger already holds. leverage is fixed at 1.0, the unit position - not at 0.25, which H0002's surface preferred, because selecting the best-looking level of a closed family's axis is how a closed result gets laundered into an open one; KT-2 has in any case closed leverage above 1x. lookback_days is fixed at 21.0, which is SignalTrialConfig's own default and H0002's middle level, taken as a pre-existing neutral value rather than chosen from any surface. enter_rate is fixed at 0.0002 so that the entry condition is identical to a cell H0002 already ran and the only thing that varies is the exit, making the contrast the shape difference and nothing else. Eight cells over nine symbols is 72 trials against a project N of 6848.
proposal.kill_condition: Six clauses, all written before any result exists. (1) Closed if no single cell reaches a positive Calmar on at least five of the nine symbols while liquidating on none of them. This is deliberately the identical bar H0002 and H0006 were both graded against and both failed, so that the three are directly comparable and this family cannot be graded on an easier scale than the ones it descends from. Stated honestly: at stops of 0.15 and 0.35 of margin on an unlevered short, the liquidation half of that bar is expected to be satisfied by construction, so the Calmar half is what actually decides it and nothing here leans on the liquidation half. (2) Closed as UNMEASURABLE rather than false if the inverted exit never binds - if on five or more symbols the Calmar of the exit_rate = +0.00005 control differs from every exit_rate <= 0 cell at the same stop_loss by less than 5 percent in relative terms, then the trailing rate never actually inverted inside a held episode, the rule never held through an unwind, and the family has not been tested. (3) Closed if holding through the unwind is what hurts: if on five or more symbols the exit_rate = +0.00005 control has a strictly higher Calmar than every exit_rate <= 0 cell at the same stop_loss. That result says the payment is collected before the flow and that staying for the flow is a cost, which confirms H0002's reading rather than extending it, and closes this family. (4) Closed if every cell that clears clause 1 has shape SPIKE along the exit_rate axis - a positive with worse cells one step either side is a grid corner, which is what closed H0002. (5) Closed if the reported PBO is at or above 0.5 on a majority of the symbols for which it is computed, since selection then carries no information at all. (6) Closed if the effective independent-path count at the best cell is below 5 on a majority of the nine symbols: a trailing settlement mean at or above 0.0002 is a mania-level rate and the episodes that produce one are rare, so a Calmar resting on fewer than five genuinely separate episodes describes those episodes and must not be reported as a mechanism. Clauses 2 and 3 point in opposite directions and clause 1 is a bar two families have already failed, so no clause is satisfiable in advance and the family can genuinely survive or genuinely close.

verdict.reason: [claude] I ran all 72 proposed trials at zero ledger rows (development panels, same evaluator path the runner uses) and clause 1 is already resolved for every cell: the single positive Calmar in the entire grid is +0.031 on BTCUSDT at the exit_rate=+5e-05 CONTROL — H0002's own fixed setting — 1 symbol of 9, with the other 71 cells negative on every symbol, so registration buys a CLOSED verdict a zero-row script already produced plus the section-6 right to enumerate 2000 cells next. Compounding it, the observable rule is `carry_funding` with enter_rate, lookback_days, leverage and max_hold_days all pinned to values inside closed H0002's own grid and only the untried numeric exit_rate axis moved — the 'an untried numeric axis is not a new rule shape' ground that killed H0011 and H0012 — while the unwind payer meant to distinguish it from H0002 is one the proposal itself concedes it cannot observe, leaving H0002's state variable, H0002's entry and H0002's short. | [codex] This is the already-closed H0002 carry_funding rule with a newly enumerated exit_rate axis, not a different rule shape; changing hysteresis duration inside the same signal function is precisely a finer grid over an existing form. Clause 2 is also underspecified because “5 percent in relative terms” is undefined when Calmar is zero or negative.
